summary.note: All seven behaviours work on a live terminal. Two MINOR deviations found inside the feature's own scope; three pre-existing issues reproduced identically on master and reported as observations, not as feature defects.

behaviours.name: Refresh interval on the first header line, changes after z
behaviours.evidence: Seeded default before any keypress: `pgcenter: 2026-08-03 08:31:40, refresh: 1s, load average: ...` (defaultRefresh = time.Second, top/config.go:14). After `z` → `3` → Enter the very next frame reads `refresh: 3s`; setting it back reads `refresh: 1s`. Header row count unchanged: 4 rows compact, sysstat 7 / pgstat 9 in verbose, matching sysstatVerboseExtra=3 / pgstatVerboseExtra=5. The master binary's line 1 reads `pgcenter: ..., load average: ...` with no refresh field, confirming the field is new.

behaviours.name: Filter indicator in the cmdline
behaviours.evidence: One filter → `[F:datname]` with `*datname` marked in the header and rows narrowed. Second filter → `[F:datname,usename]`, names in ascending column order. After six `]` presses the window hides both filtered headers (`pid  ‹backend_type ...`) and the indicator is still `[F:datname,usename]` — the footgun the indicator exists for. Survives the 2-second clear timer (sampled at t+0.15 .. t+3.5 after a message, indicator constant). Absent on the databases screen (`d`), returns on `a`. Survives help open/close and dialog open/close (`[F:usename] Set filter:` with the dialog up). An invalid regex `[a-` adds no name and leaves `[F:usename]` intact.

behaviours.name: \ clears all filters, with the three exact messages
behaviours.evidence: With two filters active, `\` prints `Filters: cleared 2 filter(s)` character for character, the indicator goes dark, the `*` markers disappear and the filtered-out rows return in the same frame. Pressed again with nothing active: `Filters: no active filters`, exact. The help screen documents the hotkey: `    \                 '\' clear all filters of the current screen.` (13-help-screen.txt line 13).
behaviours.partial: The third message, `Filters: no filter on this column`, is not observable on a live terminal — see finding O1. Marked not_verifiable, carried by a unit test.

behaviours.name: Auto-scroll brings the sort column into view
behaviours.evidence: Window opens on pid|leader|cl_addr|cl_port|datname|usename. `→` x1..x5 move the sort column across already-visible columns and the window does not move at all — no jerk. `→` x6 puts the sort column on appname, off-screen, and the window scrolls exactly one step: `pid  ‹cl_addr cl_port datname usename appname`. Continuing to the last column (`query`, index 16) brings it into the window partially and highlighted (`^[[1m^[[39mq` in the -e capture), which the user-spec counts as visible. After the auto-scroll, `]` `]` then `[` `[` `[` move the window freely to `pid  ‹backend_xid horizon_xacts xact_age query_age` with the sort column now off-screen to the right, and the window is unchanged after 7 seconds ≈ 7 refreshes — no snap-back, the request is one-shot. Pressing `→` and `S` back to back lands on procpidstat with its window at the leftmost position (no `‹` marker) — the pending request does not leak across the screen switch, including the handler that bypasses the common path.

behaviours.name: No blank line between cmdline and table in verbose; verbose engages at 12 rows
behaviours.evidence: Wide verbose: rows 1-9 are the expanded band (sysstat 7 rows, pgstat 9), row 10 is the cmdline `[F:usename]`, row 11 is the table header — the table starts on the row immediately below the cmdline, no empty row. At exactly -y 12 verbose turns ON (row 10 cmdline, row 11 table header, row 12 data). At -y 11 it falls back to compact and the indicator survives the fallback in both directions (`[F:pid]` alone and composed as `[F:pid] collecting...`).
behaviours.finding: D2 — the height-guard hint text itself is never visible. See findings.

behaviours.name: Bold values in the verbose sections; sentinels and identifiers plain
behaviours.captureMode: -p -e (escape-preserving) — the only mode that can decide this
behaviours.evidence: Both panels carry the SGR wrapper on every numeric value. sysstat: `  iostat: ESC[1mESC[37m 4ESC[0mESC[39mESC[49m devices, ESC[1mESC[37m  1ESC[0m... % max util, ...`; likewise nicstat and filesyst. pgstat: workload, databases, workers, replication, bgwr/ckpt all wrapped, e.g. `bgwr/ckpt: ESC[1mESC[37m 3/6ESC[0m... timed/req`. tmux renders the source `\033[37;1m` as `ESC[1mESC[37m`; the reset `\033[0m` arrives as `ESC[0mESC[39mESC[49m`. Sentinels are plain — `replication: ESC[1mESC[37m64.0MESC[0m... wal size,      n/a lag, ESC[1mESC[37m 0ESC[0m.../     n/a slots/retain` — the two `n/a` runs carry no escape at all. Filesystem identifier columns are plain: `filesyst: /dev/vda2 on / (ext4), ESC[1mESC[37m11.2GESC[0m... size` — device, mount point and fstype are outside any wrapper.
behaviours.note: No plain-capture fallback was used for this behaviour at any point.

behaviours.name: Dialog geometry on both axes, including the 93-character mask prompt at 80 columns
behaviours.evidence: Compact, indicator active, all three dialogs put prompt and field on one line with the field immediately after the prompt and typed input landing in it: `[F:usename] Set filter: XY`, `[F:usename] Change refresh (min 1, max 300) to 7`, `[F:usename] Enter new min age, format: HH:MM:SS[.NN]: 9`. Verbose (cmdline on row 10) is identical on all three — the axis that was hard-wired to the compact layout now follows topBandLayout, and row 11 still holds the table header, never the prompt. A prompt left untouched for 3+ seconds is still on screen, so printing it does not arm the clear timer. At 80 columns with `[F:pid]` active, `n` opens the mask dialog: the screen stays intact, every stats row keeps rendering, the prompt is cut to `[F:pid] Set state mask for group backends [a: active, i: idle, x: idl` (69 columns) leaving 11 columns for the field, typed `ai` lands in the field (`...x: idlai`) and Enter submits without disturbing the drawing. The indicator prefix is preserved ahead of the message and the field is never pushed off. The same keystroke on the master binary at the same geometry prints `set dialog view on layout failed: invalid dimensions` on the cmdline row — the teardown path this feature was written to close.
behaviours.finding: D1 — the truncated prompt carries no ellipsis. See findings.

findings.title: Truncated dialog prompt has no ellipsis
findings.observed: [F:pid] Set state mask for group backends [a: active, i: idle, x: idl
findings.expected: the user-spec requires «усекается приглашение (многоточием)» — the cut prompt should end in `…` so the user can tell the text was truncated rather than being a short prompt.
findings.analysis: truncateRunes does a hard rune cut with no marker. The important half of the criterion holds: the prompt is what gets cut, the field is not pushed off, the minimum field width is reserved and the indicator prefix survives. The tech-spec (lines 82 and 135) only says the prompt is «truncated» and never carries the ellipsis forward from the user-spec, so this looks like a requirement lost between the two documents rather than a coding slip. The indicator's own degradation ladder does emit `…`, so the two truncations are inconsistent on screen.
findings.routing: Fix belongs to Task 07's review cycle — either add the ellipsis in dialogPromptFit (note the marker must be inside the reserved budget, not added on top of it) or record an approved deviation in the decisions log and correct the user-spec wording. Not fixed here: this task has no reviewers.

findings.title: Verbose height-guard hint «terminal too short for verbose mode» never reaches the screen
findings.observed: At -y 11, pressing `v` shows `[F:pid] collecting...` and never the hint. Sampled at 0.25 s intervals from t+0.25 to t+2.5 across two toggles, and once more with the refresh interval raised to 30 s to rule out a stats tick racing in: the hint text was not observed in any frame.
findings.expected: the user-spec edge case says the layout falls back to compact «с подсказкой» — the hint should be readable at least once.
findings.analysis: One `v` keypress produces three cmdline writes: `Verbose mode: on` from toggleVerbose, `terminal too short for verbose mode` from the layout height guard, and `collecting...` from firstTickHint (which re-arms on every verbose OFF→ON by design). Each goes through printCmdline → g.Update, and gocui's Update spawns a goroutine per call, so their order is not defined; `collecting...` wins every time observed. The guard's own `verboseTooShortShown` latch is working — the message is produced, it just never survives to a frame. The fallback to compact itself is correct and the indicator coexists with whatever message wins, which is the part of the edge case that matters most.
findings.routing: Fix belongs to Task 01's review cycle. The tech-spec already names printCmdline mutual exclusion («one call per path, no overwrite») as a rule; this is a path with three calls. Not fixed here.

findings.type: observation — not a regression, reproduced on master
findings.title: Messages produced by dialogFinish never reach the cmdline
findings.owningTask: none in this feature — out of scope
findings.observed: Submitting any dialog leaves the cmdline showing only the indicator. `Filters: ok`, `Filters: regular expression cleared`, `Filters: no filter on this column`, `Refresh: ok`, the invalid-regex error and `Do nothing. Operation canceled.` were all invisible, sampled from t+0.15 s onwards. The side effects always applied correctly (refresh changed, filter set, filter cleared) — only the message is lost.
findings.analysis: dialogFinish calls printCmdline(g, "") on entry and printCmdline(g, "%s", message) on exit. gocui's Update is `go func() { g.userEvents <- ... }()`, one goroutine per call, so the empty write can be delivered after the message and blank the line. dialogFinish is byte-identical between master 4c3d555 and the feature branch, and the master binary on the same stand reproduces the same silence — this is long-standing pgcenter behaviour, not something the feature introduced.
findings.impact: It is the only reason user-spec message #3 could not be confirmed on a live terminal. Worth its own follow-up item, but fixing it is not in this feature's scope and no task owns it.

findings.type: observation — not a regression, reproduced on master
findings.title: A message printed shortly before a dialog opens wipes the prompt when its 2-second timer fires
findings.owningTask: none — the user-spec criterion as worded passes
findings.observed: `/` → Escape (which prints `Do nothing. Operation canceled.` and arms the timer) → press `z` within two seconds: the prompt renders correctly at t+0.4 s and is gone at t+1.6 s, leaving `[F:usename]` and a field with nothing to label it.
findings.analysis: The criterion is «вывод приглашения не взводит таймер очистки», and that holds: printCmdlinePersist does not arm the timer and a prompt opened after an idle gap is still on screen after 3+ seconds. What fires here is a timer armed by the previous message. The master binary shows the same sequence going blank at the same moment, so the residual case is not introduced by moving the prompt into the cmdline.
findings.impact: Cosmetic and self-inflicted only by fast keying. Reported for the record; no routing.

findings.type: observation — not a regression, reproduced on master
findings.title: Multiple filters combine as OR, not AND
findings.observed: With `datname=ppem` and `usename=postgres` active, rows whose datname is `postgres` are still printed because they match the usename filter.
findings.analysis: The loop breaks out on the first matching filter, so the row set is the union. The block is byte-identical on master 4c3d555. The indicator is truthful — both columns really do carry active filters, and both are marked `*` in the header.
findings.impact: Not a defect of this feature, but the indicator makes multi-filter state visible for the first time, so users will now notice the semantics. Worth a roadmap note rather than a fix here.
